Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

partly adverb

also in part, partially, to some extent, partly … partly

classical

Cic. Marc. 1: partim dolōre, partim verēcundiā (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Q. fr. 1.3.5: amīcī partim dēseruerint mē, partim etiam prōdiderint (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 136

partim

adverb: an old accusative of pars

partly; partim … partim, partly … partly

Most often doubled, partim … partim, “partly … partly”, and with persons “some … others” (amīcī partim … partim, some of my friends … others). In Plautus and Cato it can mean “for the most part” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ex parte — in part, partly

    phrase: ex with the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.9: ex parte gaudeō (Lewis & Short)

    With an adjective it gives the degree: aliquā ex parte, to some extent; magnā ex parte, largely (see largely); nē minimā quidem ex parte, not in the least (Cic. Off. 1.76, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • diūturnī silentiī … nōn timōre aliquō, sed partim dolōre, partim verēcundiā, fīnem hodiernus diēs attulit

    today has brought an end to a long silence, kept not from any fear but partly from grief, partly from diffidenceCic. Marc. 1 (Lewis & Short)

  • multa ab animālium vōcibus trālāta in hominēs, partim quae sunt aperta, partim obscūra

    many words have been carried over from the cries of animals to people, some of them plain, some obscureVarr. LL 7.103

  • dīcere etiam solēbat nūllum esse librum tam malum ut nōn aliquā parte prōdesset

    he used to say, too, that no book was so bad that it was not useful in some partPlin. Ep. 3.5.10

See also largely, part, half.
